extracted.intended_audience: Navy field activity comptrollers and newly reported Navy financial managers responsible for OMB Circular A-76 (Commercial Activities) studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for Navy field activity comptrollers to plan, conduct, document, and monitor OMB Circular A-76 Commercial Activities (CA) studies and resulting contracting/most-efficient-organization decisions. Focus is on practical steps, required knowledge, regulatory compliance, and management practices to achieve efficiency and control budget impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Work (Performance Work Statement) formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Performance Work Statement specifies acceptable standards and quality levels to be achieved and should describe personnel requirements, equipment requirements, performance standards and other criteria which both the government and commercial source are expected to meet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper formulation of the Statement of Work (SOW) is paramount: it must be clear, concise, complete, and include all functions now performed by government employees. Omitting functions lets contractors undercut government costs, produces unperformed work that must be shifted to other personnel, may cause costly change orders, and undermines contract quality. Training in SOW development is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate Cost Comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost comparison develops estimates of government performance costs and compares them to commercial source performance costs for a commercial activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost comparisons must capture all costs (direct, indirect, overhead) and be based on accurate research and computation. Inaccurate cost comparisons, improper research, or incorrect computations can yield poor decisions. Comptrollers should ensure costing procedures capture all costs associated with the function being studied and periodically monitor cost trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination and monitoring of the Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: MEO is the government organization structured to perform the activity as efficiently as practical and is compared against commercial offers in the CA study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper determination of the MEO is required; if MEO is chosen over a contractor, the activity must monitor the MEO post-award to ensure it remains cost efficient. MEO costings must be accurate and documented like commercial bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to OMB Circular A-76 and acquisition regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 sets policy and procedures for performance of commercial activities and directs evaluations of whether services should be contracted out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptrollers must be familiar with OMB A-76, its supplements, and the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) system (and predecessor DAR/DAR history), and ensure implementation follows A-76 steps, policy, and procedures for fairness and proper evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with applicable laws and statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition and contracting are governed by a framework of laws, GAO/OMB/congressional decisions, and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptrollers should be aware of and apply relevant statutes (examples listed: Budget and Accounting Act, Competition in Contracting Act, Truth in Negotiations, Prompt Payment Act, Buy American, Small Business Act, Davis-Bacon, Service Contract Act, etc.). Awareness of socio-economic laws and updating for legislative changes is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation to justify contracting decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation must justify management’s decision to contract out or retain the service in-house and serve as the benchmark for contract compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper and sufficient documentation is essential to withstand GAO, Congressional, and upper-echelon review. Post-award documentation should substantiate contractor noncompliance, performance trends, and reasons for decisions; inadequate documentation leaves the activity vulnerable to criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensive up-front planning for CA studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial Activity studies require intensive up-front planning to ensure accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up-front planning should identify all functions/costs, ensure the SOW is comprehensive, and set benchmarks for later monitoring. Planning reduces errors that lead to inefficient outcomes and budget impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluid communication within activity and with contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluid communication between all parties in the A-76 process reduces confusion, mistrust and misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain open internal communication among comptroller, management analysts, and studied departments, and open lines with contractors for feedback and performance improvement. Communication mitigates negative attitudes and improves data quality for CA studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and adequate staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient, adequately trained and qualified personnel are required to maintain the A-76 process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel need training in SOW formulation, CA study conduct, contracting administration, and monitoring. Activities often lack qualified staff; investing in training and staffing is recommended to administer the program effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and contract administration (post-award follow-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring should include a comparison of actual versus projected results and periodic evaluation of the quality and cost of services provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow up on contracts to ensure contractors meet contract specifications; monitor performance and costs, document discrepancies, and ensure both contractors and, if applicable, MEOs remain cost-efficient over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of contracting method (sealed bid vs. competitive negotiation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two major methods are sealed bidding and competitive negotiation; each has admission criteria and procedural steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sealed bidding where time permits, awards can be made on price/price-related factors, discussions are unnecessary, and multiple bids are expected. Use negotiation where sealed bid criteria cannot be met; negotiation involves proposals, discussions, and cost/pricing data when thresholds apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of contract type (fixed-price vs cost-reimbursement) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract type selection depends on degree/timing of cost risk assumed by contractor and incentives for performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider price competition, cost and price analyses, urgency, complexity, and contractor accounting system adequacy when selecting contract types (e.g., firm-fixed-price, fixed-price redeterminable, cost-reimbursement). Choose to allocate risk and incentives appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole-source contracting justification and statutory exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sole-source contracts are permitted under seven statutory exceptions but require formal justification and approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper identification of exceptions (only one responsible source, urgency, industrial mobilization, international agreements, statutory requirements, national security, public interest) and obtain required approvals and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance standards, quality levels, and measurable acceptance criteria in PWS
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS should specify acceptable standards and quality levels to be achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define measurable performance standards, personnel qualifications, equipment, and acceptance criteria so contractor performance can be objectively evaluated and monitored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and quantification of loss of management flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 contracts can reduce managers’ flexibility to reallocate resources to meet emergent requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and, where practical, quantify the value of managerial flexibility in CA studies so decisions weigh cost savings against operational constraints. Ensure SOW captures necessary flexibility or plan for contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor cost accounting and audit readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting requires contractors to have adequate accounting systems; DCAA audits contractor books and records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For negotiated contracts (and where cost data thresholds apply), require cost/pricing data, assess contractor accounting system adequacy, and plan for DCAA audit involvement. Inadequate accounting increases government risk and price uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of commercial activity vs inherently governmental functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial activity: provides a product/service obtainable from commercial sources; Governmental function: so intimately related to public interest that government must perform it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully identify whether activities are commercial (food services, ADP, admin services) or inherently governmental (discretionary application of government authority, monetary transactions, maintenance of in-house technical core). Only commercial activities are candidates for CA study and conversion to contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of socio-economic and public policy obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement must accomplish public goals and abide by socio-economic laws (small business goals, Buy American, service contract provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate socio-economic requirements and any set-asides or subcontracting obligations into CA studies, SOW, and evaluations; these can affect cost and contractor selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget impact awareness and resource allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Savings from A-76 contracts are deleted from the activity’s budget and affect resource availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptrollers must understand how A-76 outcomes affect budget formulation and execution, allocate resources accordingly, and be prepared to defend budget requests when savings reduce activity funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder attitude management and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers and employees often view A-76 negatively due to job loss and reduced flexibility; this affects participation and data quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage stakeholders early, communicate transparently to reduce bias/defensiveness, and obtain accurate data for CA studies. Management tips include proactive involvement and education to mitigate resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic monitoring of cost trends to ensure continued efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers must monitor cost trends from year to year to ensure the commercial source remains more cost efficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish procedures for annual or periodic review of contractor and MEO costs and performance to detect erosion of projected savings and take corrective action if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and qualification of contracting personnel (PCO, ACO, TCO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers must be knowledgeable and qualified, selected based on experience, training, and area expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contracting officers have requisite training/qualifications; involve Procurement Contracting Officer (award), Administrative Contracting Officer (performance monitoring), and Termination Contracting Officer (settlement of terminated contracts) appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of special contracting methods when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Special methods (multi-year, options, leader company contracts) exist to increase economic efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate special contracting vehicles for their objectives, limitations, and requirements; select them only when they serve cost-efficiency and program needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture full spectrum of costs to avoid omitted-function underbidding
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to include all functions in the SOW or to capture all costs allows bidders to undercut government estimates and win contracts without performing all necessary work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure CA studies and SOW include incidental and peripheral tasks, change-order risks, transition costs, and any hidden costs to avoid future cost increases and degraded service quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite knowledge for financial managers in A-76 administration
rubrics_metrics.description: A working/practical knowledge of A-76 process, applicable laws/regulations, contracting process, and the comptroller’s role is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptrollers should learn: what OMB Circular A-76 is, key statutes/regulations guiding managers, the contracting process under A-76, and how the comptroller’s role can be improved. Level of knowledge depends on command size and role in the process.
